messages.content:
Build the app described below in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Tailwind CSS v4 with shadcn/ui (new-york style, neutral theme) is set up, every shadcn/ui component is already installed under `@/components/ui/*`, lucide-react is installed, sonner's `<Toaster />` is mounted in the root layout, and the shadcn/ui documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/README.md`).

Task: Lumen needs a command palette. Inside a shared app layout with three screens (a dashboard at `/`, projects at `/projects`, members at `/members`), pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) opens a palette with a search field. Results are grouped under "Pages" (the three screens), "Actions" ("Create project", "Invite member", "Toggle theme") and "Recent" (three recently opened projects). Typing filters every group; arrow keys move the highlight and Enter runs it. "Invite member" opens a dialog with an email field. A visible button in the header (with the shortcut shown next to it) opens the palette too, so it works on phones.

Requirements:
- The app must serve these routes: `/`, `/projects`, `/members`. Each route default-exports its page from its `page.tsx`; nested layouts are allowed.
- Write as many files as the app needs, under `app/`, `components/` or `lib/`. Do not change any file that already exists in the project except `app/page.tsx`. The root layout, global styles and the stack's standard providers already exist. You can read the project's existing files under `project/`.
- Put "use client" at the top of every file that uses state, effects or event handlers.
- Use realistic placeholder content defined in the files (no lorem ipsum). Load nothing from the network: no external image, font or API URLs.
- The app must type-check under strict TypeScript, pass `next build`, and render every route without console errors.
- Make it responsive from phone to desktop, and accessible.
- Reply with every file, each in its own fenced code block whose opening line names the file's path, like ```tsx app/settings/page.tsx, and nothing else.

content.content:
# shadcn/ui documentation (local copy)

This folder is a local copy of the shadcn/ui documentation and agent skill, pinned to one
commit of github.com/shadcn-ui/ui. Everything listed here is already set up in the project.

- `skill/SKILL.md`: the official shadcn/ui agent skill (rules in `skill/rules/`). The
  shadcn CLI is **not** available in this environment: every component is already
  installed under `@/components/ui/*`, so skip any step that says to run `npx shadcn`.
- `llms.txt`: the official documentation index. A link of the form
  `https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/<name>` is available here as
  `components/<name>.mdx`.
- `components/*.mdx`: per-component docs (Radix flavour, matching the installed components).
  A `<ComponentPreview name="x" />` tag refers to the example source in `examples/x.tsx`.
- `examples/*.tsx`: the example source behind each docs preview.
- `blocks/`: the official shadcn/ui blocks (dashboard, login, sidebar, ...).
- `installation/next.mdx`: Next.js setup notes (already done).

Imports in `examples/` and `blocks/` have been rewritten to the project's paths
(`@/components/ui/*`, `@/lib/utils`, `@/hooks/*`), as the shadcn CLI does.

## About

The `<Command />` component uses the [`cmdk`](https://github.com/dip/cmdk) component by [Dip](https://www.dip.org/).

## Installation

<CodeTabs>

<TabsList>
  <TabsTrigger value="cli">Command</TabsTrigger>
  <TabsTrigger value="manual">Manual</TabsTrigger>
</TabsList>
<TabsContent value="cli">

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add command
```

</TabsContent>

<TabsContent value="manual">

<Steps className="mb-0 pt-2">

<Step>Install the following dependencies:</Step>

```bash
npm install cmdk
```

<Step>Copy and paste the following code into your project.</Step>

<ComponentSource
  name="command"
  title="components/ui/command.tsx"
  styleName="radix-nova"
/>

<Step>Update the import paths to match your project setup.</Step>

</Steps>

</TabsContent>

</CodeTabs>

## Usage

```tsx showLineNumbers
import {
  Command,
  CommandDialog,
  CommandEmpty,
  CommandGroup,
  CommandInput,
  CommandItem,
  CommandList,
  CommandSeparator,
  CommandShortcut,
} from "@/components/ui/command"
```

```tsx showLineNumbers
<Command className="max-w-sm rounded-lg border">
  <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandGroup heading="Suggestions">
      <CommandItem>Calendar</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem>Search Emoji</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem>Calculator</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
    <CommandSeparator />
    <CommandGroup heading="Settings">
      <CommandItem>Profile</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem>Billing</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem>Settings</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
  </CommandList>
</Command>
```

## Composition

Use the following composition to build a `Command`:

```text
Command
├── CommandInput
└── CommandList
    ├── CommandEmpty
    ├── CommandGroup
    │   ├── CommandItem
    │   └── CommandItem
    ├── CommandSeparator
    └── CommandGroup
        ├── CommandItem
        └── CommandItem
```
